draft.title: The Cartesian plane
card: The Cartesian plane has a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis. They cross at the origin, the point \((0, 0)\). The axes split the plane into four quadrants.
A point is written as \((x, y)\). To plot it, start at the origin. Move across first (right if \(x\) is positive, left if negative). Then move up or down for \(y\) (up if positive, down if negative).
For \((-3, 2)\): go 3 units left, then 2 units up. The point is in the upper left quadrant.
The order matters. \((2, 5)\) and \((5, 2)\) are different points. A point on an axis has a 0 in its pair, such as \((4, 0)\).

1.alt: A Cartesian plane with the x-axis and y-axis from \(-5\) to \(5\), crossing at the origin. Quadrant labels 1 to 4 are in the upper right, upper left, lower left and lower right.

3.alt: The point \((-3, 2)\) plotted 3 units left and 2 units up from the origin.

draft.remember: Across first, then up or down: \((x, y)\) in that order.

a.q: Which description shows how to plot the point \((-4, 3)\)?
a.why: The first number is \(x\). It is negative, so move 4 units left. The second number is \(y\). It is positive, so move 3 units up. Starting with 3 units left swaps the order of the pair.
a.clue: Move across first, using the first number.

b.q: Mia plots the point \((5, -2)\) on a Cartesian plane. Where does it lie?
opts: 5 right of the y-axis, 2 below the x-axis
5 left of the y-axis, 2 below the x-axis
2 right of the y-axis, 5 below the x-axis
5 right of the y-axis, 2 above the x-axis
b.why: The \(x\) value of 5 puts the point 5 units right of the y-axis. The \(y\) value of \(-2\) puts it 2 units below the x-axis. Reading 2 as the across move swaps the two numbers.
b.clue: Positive \(x\) goes right. Negative \(y\) goes down.

b.best: 5 right of the y-axis, 2 below the x-axis
